title.value: Physics-Guided Adversarial Machine Learning for Aircraft Systems Simulation
title.justification: The title accurately represents the main focus of the paper, which is the development of a novel physics-guided adversarial machine learning approach for aircraft systems simulation.
title.quote: This work presents a novel approach, physics-guided adversarial machine learning (ML), that improves the confidence over the physics consistency of the model.

extractions.description: The paper introduces a physics-guided adversarial machine learning approach to enhance the reliability of machine learning models used in aircraft systems simulation. This method combines adversarial testing with physics-informed training to ensure the consistency of model predictions with physics domain knowledge, aiming to improve trust in ML-based systems for aircraft performance assessment.

primary_category.justification: The paper primarily focuses on advancements in machine learning techniques for the aviation industry, without specific emphasis on eco-responsible AI categories related to climate, environment, or sustainability from the provided hierarchy.
primary_category.quote: The objective is to assess how effective our approach is at testing the physics consistency of a DNN by exposing adversarial examples that highlight problematic regions in the input space, where the model deviates from the foreknown domain knowledge.

primary_sub_category.justification: The paper does not align with any of the listed eco-responsible sub-categories as its primary focus is on improving the trustworthiness of ML models for aircraft systems, rather than addressing specific environmental or sustainability issues.
primary_sub_category.quote: This work presents a novel approach, physics-guided adversarial machine learning (ML), that improves the confidence over the physics consistency of the model.

new_primary_category.justification: This category is suggested because the paper focuses on improving the reliability and performance of machine learning models within aerospace systems, specifically for aircraft systems simulation, which is not covered by the existing categories.
new_primary_category.quote: The effectiveness evaluation of our proposed testing approach was conducted on two industrial cases of aircraft system performance models.

new_primary_sub_category.justification: This sub-category is suggested because the primary focus of the paper is on enhancing the simulation and modeling of aerospace systems using physics-informed machine learning approaches.
